solutions.approach_name: Total Sum and Running Prefix Sum

analysis.problem_summary: Find the leftmost index in an array where the sum of elements strictly to the left equals the sum of elements strictly to the right.
analysis.intuition: If we know the total sum of the array in advance, the sum of elements to the right of index `i` is simply `total_sum - left_sum - nums[i]`. Thus, we can evaluate whether `i` is a pivot in O(1) time while iterating through the array.
approach: Compute the total sum of all elements in the array in a first pass.
Initialize `leftSum` to 0 and set `rightSum` to the computed total sum.
Iterate through each index `i` from left to right.
Check if `leftSum == rightSum - nums[i]`. If equal, return index `i` immediately.
Otherwise, update `leftSum += nums[i]` and `rightSum -= nums[i]` before continuing to the next element.
If no pivot index is found after checking all elements, return -1.
analysis.why_it_works: At any index `i`, the remaining sum to the right is equal to `totalSum - leftSum - nums[i]`. By incrementally tracking `leftSum`, we check the equality condition in constant time per element.
analysis.key_takeaway: Pre-calculating global properties (like array total sum) allows converting nested traversal problems into linear O(N) running sum inspections.
analysis.time_explanation: The algorithm computes the total sum in one O(n) pass, then inspects each element in a second O(n) pass. Overall time complexity is linear, O(n).
analysis.space_explanation: Only a constant number of scalar variable integer accumulators (`leftSum` and `rightSum`) are used, giving O(1) auxiliary space complexity.

solutions.approach_name: Brute Force Left and Right Sum Calculation

analysis.problem_summary: Determine the first index where the sum of elements to its left equals the sum of elements to its right.
analysis.intuition: For each index `i`, directly iterate over all elements to its left to compute `leftSum`, and all elements to its right to compute `rightSum`, then compare the two.
approach: Loop through each index `i` from 0 to `nums.length - 1`.
For the current index `i`, iterate through all elements from index `0` to `i - 1` to calculate `leftSum`.
Iterate through all elements from index `i + 1` to `nums.length - 1` to calculate `rightSum`.
If `leftSum == rightSum`, return `i` as the leftmost pivot index.
If the loop finishes without finding a valid index, return -1.
analysis.why_it_works: The algorithm directly computes the exact sums specified in the definition for every candidate index, guaranteeing correctness by brute force.
analysis.key_takeaway: While correct, re-summing sub-arrays independently for each index leads to quadratic time complexity, which can be optimized using running prefix sums.
analysis.time_explanation: For each index `i`, the code iterates over all `n` elements across two inner loops. Summing `n` times for `n` candidates yields O(n^2) time overall.
analysis.space_explanation: The calculation uses only primitive variables for `leftSum` and `rightSum`, requiring constant O(1) auxiliary space.
